member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.Tint
member.summary: Car paint tints from JC3's general_palette_muted (.vmodc). Cars layer a mask over the diffuse: where the mask red channel is high the body shows a chosen tint colour, where it's black the diffuse shows through. The viewer picks one of these tints (deterministically per model) to stand in for the game's random colour. Values are the primary (tint_r) variant, linear RGB.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.CarTints.Pick(System.Int32)
member.summary: Pick a tint deterministically from a seed (e.g. the model path hash) so a given car always gets the same colour within a session, but different cars differ. Use a random seed for true randomness.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.CharacterDecoder
member.summary:
Decoders for the Character and CharacterSkin render blocks (skinned character meshes). Both use one of six packed vertex layouts selected by flag bits; we read position (int16 SNORM) and the first UV set, skip bone weights/indices and extra UV sets, and decode the packed tangent. Skin batches are skipped (not needed for static display).
Character: version + CharacterAttributes(0x6C) + materials + vbuf + skin batches + indices. CharacterSkin: same shape, CharacterSkinAttributes size differs.
Vertex stride index = 3*bit1 + bit4 + bit5 (bitN = bit N of flags), indexing VertexStrides {0x18,0x1C,0x20,0x20,0x24,0x28}. Indices 0-2 are 4-bone (8 bytes bone data), 3-5 are 8-bone (16 bytes). After bone data come 1/2/3 UV sets (int16 pairs) then a uint32 packed tangent.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.CollisionMesh

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.CollisionModel

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.CollisionReader

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.GeneralBlockDecoder

Decoder for the General render-block family (General, GeneralJC3, GeneralMkIII and the masked variant). These cover the overwhelming majority of static world/prop geometry, which is why they are the v1 scope. Buffer layout per buffer: u32 element-count, then count*stride bytes.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.GeneralBlockDecoder.Decode(JustCause.Models.Core.LeReader,System.UInt32,JustCause.Models.Core.RenderBlock)

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.GltfExporter
member.summary: Exports an RbmModel to glTF 2.0 (.gltf + .bin). One mesh primitive per render block, carrying POSITION, NORMAL, TANGENT, TEXCOORD_0 (UV0) and TEXCOORD_1 (UV1) - the second UV set is why we use glTF over OBJ, so paintjob/decal setups that sample UV1 survive the export. Materials reference PNG textures by relative URI (image writing is the caller's job; this only records the references).

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.GltfExporter.BlockMaterial
member.summary: Per-block material: relative PNG URIs for every map the block uses. Base color + normal go in the standard glTF slots (UV0); the game-specific maps (tint mask, decal, paintjob) are recorded in material "extras" with their image URI and UV set index, so they survive into Blender for manual wiring - glTF's PBR material has no standard slot for them, but the images and the UV channels are all present.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.GltfExporter.Export(JustCause.Models.Core.RbmModel,System.Collections.Generic.IList{JustCause.Models.Core.GltfExporter.BlockMaterial},System.String,System.Byte[]@)
member.summary: Build the glTF. materials[i] corresponds to model.Blocks[i] (may be null for a block with no textures). binPath is the .bin file name referenced by the .gltf (relative). Returns the .gltf JSON text; the .bin bytes come back via the out parameter.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.MdicInstance
member.summary: One placed model instance: which model, and its 4x4 world transform.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.MdicFile
member.summary:
JC3 .mdic (Model Instance Dictionary) - places structure/base models in the world. Layout ported from the JC3 toolset (Gibbed.JustCause3.ConvertLocationData/ ModelInstanceDictionary.cs):
0x00 u32 magic 'MDI\0' (0x0049444D) 0x04 u32 version 0x08 u32 modelCount 0x0C u32 instanceCount 0x10 u32 matrixOffset (relative to 0x20) 0x14 u32,u32,u32 (preserved header fields) 0x20 string table: modelCount null-terminated latin1 model paths 0x20+matrixOffset matrix array: instanceCount x 16 floats (4x4, column-major) then u16 modelIndex[instanceCount] then u16 flag[instanceCount] then header array: instanceCount x 4 floats then AABB array: instanceCount x 6 floats (min xyz, max xyz)
We read the model paths, per-instance transform, and model index - enough to place each model in the scene. The flag/header/AABB arrays aren't needed for previewing.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.ObjExporter
member.summary: Exports a decoded model to Wavefront OBJ. One group per render block. Positions, UVs (v flipped for OBJ convention) and normals are written when present. Materials are referenced by name; texture resolution is the caller's job (the viewer wires this to the texture core).

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.ObjExporter.Export(JustCause.Models.Core.CollisionModel)
member.summary: Export a collision model to Wavefront OBJ. One group per convex/mesh piece, named by its surface material. Faces are polygons (OBJ supports n-gons natively). No UVs/normals (collision has none).

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.Packing.UnpackNormal(System.Single,System.Single@,System.Single@,System.Single@)

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.LeReader
member.summary: Thin little-endian reader over a byte span. The reference uses raw std::istream.read into packed structs; we read field-by-field so struct packing/endianness is never ambiguous across platforms.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.LeReader.ReadLengthPrefixedString

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.RbmHeader

member.name: P:JustCause.Models.Core.RenderBlock.NormalTexture

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.ModelVariant
member.summary: The parsed model: header + ordered blocks. The viewer's unit of work.

Which JC3 content generation a model comes from. Detected from block versions during parsing: the 2015-06-24 beta build uses older block versions (GeneralMkIII v3, CharacterSkin v5, CarPaintMM v13) than the shipped game (v5 / v6 / v14). Blocks that don't differ between builds (e.g. Character v9) carry no signal, so a model is only tagged Beta when a beta-versioned block is actually seen; otherwise it defaults to Final.

member.name: P:JustCause.Models.Core.RbmModel.VariantTag

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.RbmParser
member.summary:
Parses an RBMDL container into an . v1 decodes the General render-block family; any other recognised block is named and skipped with a warning rather than aborting the parse, so a model that mixes General geometry with (say) a decal block still shows its geometry.
Philosophy mirrors the texture core's tolerant reader: never hard-fail on a version mismatch (the reference __debugbreak()s); warn and continue.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.RenderBlockNames
member.summary: Maps RBM block hashes to friendly names. The full table is kept (not just the decodable blocks) so that when an undecoded block is skipped, the warning can name it precisely - "skipped FogVolume" instead of "skipped 0xB0E85383". Generated from the reference render_block_factory.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.RoadJunctionDecoder
member.summary:
RenderBlockRoadJunction (hash 0x566DCE92, version 1). The reference renderer (jc-model-renderer) only NAMES this block type in its factory and has no decoder, so this layout was reverse-engineered from real files (bridge_tiles_train_span_48):
u8 version (== 1) attributes (0xFC bytes) - includes a float position scale at +0x08 materials (count-prefixed string list + float[4] MaterialParams) u32 vertexCount vertex stream 1: PackedVertexPosition-style, 16B stride (int16 x,y,z + 10B skin/pad we don't need) u32 vertexCount (again) vertex stream 2: 20B stride (packed UV/normal - not decoded yet) u32 indexCount index stream: u16 indices
We decode positions (int16 * scale) and indices - enough to render the tile. The second stream (UV/normal) is skipped for now; positions render with a flat normal. Scale is per-file (48.0 for the 48m span tile).

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.ShieldDecoder
member.summary:
RenderBlockBavariumShield (hash 0xA5D24CCD) - the energy shield mesh used by vehicle shields. The reference renderer only NAMES this block; the layout here is taken from the Blender importer (io_import_rbm/import_bavarium_shield.py), which is the authoritative behavioural reference:
u8 version float[4] material data u32 filepathSlotCount, then that many length-prefixed strings (textures) 16 bytes (skipped) u32 vertexCount vertex (28B): float x,y,z ; float u,v (v negated) ; u32 normal ; u32 tangent u32 indexCount ; u16 indices[indexCount] u32 endstring
Normal/tangent are the standard Avalanche packed-normal floats (UnpackNormal).

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.WaterHullDecoder
member.summary:
RenderBlockWaterHull (hash 0xF99C72A1) - a simple hull mesh (position-only). Layout from the Blender importer (io_import_rbm/import_water_hull.py):
21 bytes (skipped - version + attributes) u32 vertexCount vertex (12B): float x,y,z (no UVs/normals/textures) u32 indexCount ; u16 indices[indexCount] u32 endstring
Normals aren't stored, so the viewer synthesises them from the geometry.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.WaterMaskDecoder
member.summary: RenderBlockWaterMask (hash 0x90FE086C) - a boat/vehicle water-displacement mask. Byte-identical layout to WaterHull (verified on sailboat_water_mask_lod1: 21-byte skip, u32 vertCount, position-only 12B vertices, u32 idxCount, u16 indices, then the 0x89ABCDEF end marker). The reference renderer names it ("WaterMask") but doesn't decode it, and there's no Blender importer - RE'd from the file.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureKinds
member.summary: Maps an Apex texture path to a human-readable "kind" for the UI (Diffuse Map, Normal Map, etc.), inferred from the filename suffix. The suffix convention is stable across JC3 (_dif/_nrm/_mpm/_mask/...); slot-based meaning (paintjob, decal) is handled separately by the block, since those don't always carry a suffix.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureKinds.DescribeSlot(System.UInt32,System.Int32,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Slot-aware label. When the block type + slot index have a known name (from the shader register table), that name is authoritative and is used regardless of the filename. Otherwise falls back to suffix inference. selects the eye body-part layout for Character blocks (a compact Diffuse + Reflection pair).

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureKinds.Describe(System.String)
member.summary: Human-readable label for a texture path (e.g. "Normal Map").

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureResolver
member.summary:
Resolves a model's archive-relative texture paths (e.g. "models/jc_props/easteregg/textures/banana_stand_dif.ddsc" or the shared "textures/dummies/dummy_black.ddsc") to real files on disk.
Contract: the user has extracted the whole game with matching .ddsc, so the on-disk layout mirrors the archive layout. A model therefore sits at {root}/models/.../foo.rbm and every texture - whether a sibling under the model's own textures/ folder or a SHARED texture elsewhere - resolves as {root}/{archive-relative-path}. So textures are resolved against the ROOT, never against the model's own directory.
Root discovery: the folder above the top-level "models" segment of the model's path. If the model isn't under a "models" segment, or the first texture doesn't resolve there, no root is found and textures are skipped (the "opened from outside a game unpack" case - handled later via the live-update assign feature).

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureResolver.ForRoot(System.String)
member.summary: Build a resolver rooted at an explicit folder (e.g. a user-picked beta files root). Archive-relative texture paths resolve directly beneath it. Returns HasRoot=false if the folder is null/absent.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureResolver.ForModel(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Resolve a texture root for a model. When is true, a self-contained unpacked AAF is treated as its own full unpack: the partial-unpack marker (@files.xml) is ignored and the local root is used directly, so bundled textures load from the AAF itself rather than the game install. Used when authoring custom vehicles/items where everything lives in one AAF.

member.name: M:JustCause.Models.Core.TextureResolver.Resolve(System.String)
member.summary: Resolve one archive-relative texture path to a full disk path, or null if there's no root or the file doesn't exist.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.VegetationDecoder
member.summary:
Decoder for the two undocumented JC3 vegetation render blocks (0xB1F9133D and 0xD79884C6), reverse-engineered from real files (neither the jc-model-renderer nor Gibbed implements these). Both share the same geometry layout and differ only in attribute size:
version (1 byte) attributes: 0xB1F9133D = 51 floats (204 B); 0xD79884C6 = 24 floats (96 B) materials (standard: u32 count + length-prefixed names + 16-byte params) header: float scale? + float uvExtentX + float uvExtentY + u32 pad vbuf1: u32 count + count * 12 bytes (int16 x,y,z + 6 bytes normal/data) vbuf2: u32 count + count * 8 bytes (packed UV) indices: u32 count + count * u16 end marker
Positions are int16 SNORM (value/32767 in [-1,1]) scaled by the model's largest bounding-box half-extent (uniform scale reproduces all axes). UV0 is read from vbuf2 as int16 SNORM * uvExtent.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.VehicleDecoder
member.summary:
Decoders for the CarPaintMM and CarLight vehicle render blocks. Both use all-float (unpacked) vertex data in one of three flag-selected layouts: plain, skinned, or deform. We read positions and the UV/normal stream; skin batches and deform weights are skipped (display only).
CarPaintMM: version + CarPaintMMAttributes(0x8) + StaticMaterialParams(316) + DynamicMaterialParams(76) + deform table(1024) + materials + vbufs + [skin batch if skinned] + [layered UV if SUPPORT_LAYERED|OVERLAY] + indices. CarLight: version + CarLightAttributes(0x3C) + deform table(1024) + materials + vbufs + [skin batch if skinned] + indices.
Vertex streams (by flags): skinned: UnpackedVertexWithNormal1 (x,y,z,n floats, 0x10) + UnpackedNormals deform: VertexDeformPos (x,y,z,d + 4 int16 weights, 0x18) + VertexDeformNormal2 plain: UnpackedVertexPosition (x,y,z, 0xC) + UnpackedNormals (UVs+n+t, 0x18) UV0 is the first two floats of the second (data) stream.

member.name: T:JustCause.Models.Core.WindowLandmarkDecoder
member.summary:
Decoders for the Window and Landmark render blocks. Both are low-complexity (no skin batches, no deform tables) and reuse the same vertex primitives as the General family.
Window: version + WindowAttributes(0x28) + materials + UnpackedVertexPosition2UV buffer + indices. All-float, like the General unpacked path. Landmark: version + LandmarkAttributes(0x58, carries SPackedAttribute) + materials + PackedVertexPosition buffer + PackedTexWithSomething buffer + indices. Packed int16 positions like the General packed path; UV is int16 SNORM * uv0Extent.
